title: FDA: Fourier domain adaptation for semantic segmentation
relevance: Bridges a domain gap by swapping only the LOW-FREQUENCY AMPLITUDE spectrum between source and target images - no training, no labels, no adversarial stage - because amplitude carries style (texture, colour, contrast) while phase carries semantic content. This attacks our consensus finding (a) head-on: augmentation spans 8x GSD but not the King contractor change or the sensor switch, and those are exactly style, i.e. amplitude. It is the cheapest intervention found in this entire loop - an FFT per tile - and it is directly testable on 2000 vs 2020 before any retraining. It also implies the per-year low-frequency amplitude summary IS the sensor-era signature, giving the low-dimensional feature space that Search 20's reweighting needs.
